title: Domicile Certificate 2026: How to Apply, Documents, Uses
meta_description: Domicile certificate online 2026 - state-wise application portals, documents, processing time 7-15 days. Required for state government jobs and education.

hero.one_liner: Domicile certificate proves your permanent residence in a state - essential for state government jobs, state university quota, and state-specific schemes

sections.heading: What a Domicile Certificate Is and When You Need It
content: A domicile certificate is official proof that you are a permanent resident of a particular state. It confirms your home state for the purpose of state-level benefits.

It is critical for state government jobs, where most state PSCs, police, and teaching posts require domicile proof. It is also the key to state university quota seats, which can be 85 to 90% of college seats.
Many state schemes are domicile-only, like Ladli Behna and Kanya Sumangala. Domicile also matters for some state tenders and agricultural land rules.
Unlike caste or income certificates, domicile is purely about which state you belong to, not your category or earnings.
Because states reserve a large share of jobs and college seats for their own residents, this one document quietly decides a lot of opportunities.
It is issued by the state revenue authority and then asked for repeatedly through your education and career, so getting it early saves trouble later.
For students especially, having it ready well before counselling can be the difference between a state quota seat and missing out.

sections.title: Domicile vs Residence Certificate: Don't Mix Them Up
sections.content:
A domicile certificate proves your permanent home state, used for job and education quotas and state schemes. A residence certificate only proves your current address and is used for voter ID or local services.

Domicile carries more legal weight and usually lasts a lifetime. Residence is temporary, often valid for just 1 to 6 months.

Many students wrongly apply for residence when they actually need domicile.

sections.heading: Domicile vs Residence at a Glance

rows.label: Domicile Certificate
rows.value: Proves your PERMANENT home state - where you intend to settle. Valid even if you move to another state temporarily. Permanent/lifetime validity. Used for government jobs, education quota, state schemes.

rows.label: Residence Certificate
rows.value: Proves you CURRENTLY LIVE at a specific address. Valid only for that address. Usually valid for 1-6 months (limited scope). Used for voter registration, local municipal benefits, temporary address proof.

rows.label: When to Use Which
rows.value: Government job/education: Domicile. Local address update: Residence. Scheme eligibility: Check - most state schemes require domicile, some may accept residence. Always verify the specific requirement.

items.sub: Mandatory in most states for online filing.

sections.heading: How to Apply Online, Step by Step

steps.title: Open your state portal
steps.desc: Go to your state e-District portal, like edistrict.up.gov.in or aaplesarkar.mahaonline.gov.in.

steps.title: Fill the form
steps.desc: Register, select Domicile Certificate, and enter your personal and address details.

steps.title: Upload and pay
steps.desc: Upload Aadhaar, address proof, and residence proof, then pay the small fee.

steps.title: Verify and issue
steps.desc: A Patwari may verify your address, then the SDM approves and issues the certificate.

sections.heading: The Application Process in Detail
content: Fill the form with your full name, address, and residence period, then upload documents as PDF or JPG within the size limit. Pay the fee of Rs 10 to 100 by UPI, net banking, or card.
Save the application reference number, since you will need it to track status. In many states a local Tehsildar or Patwari does a field verification before approval.
Offline, you collect the form at the Tehsildar or SDM office and submit it with copies. Online is faster and trackable, usually 7 to 15 days against 15 to 30 offline.
The issuing authority is an officer such as the Tehsildar, SDM, or District Magistrate, so check that the certificate carries an authorised signature.
For central use you may need it in a prescribed format, which can differ from the plain state version, so confirm the format your exam asks for.
Track the status on the portal using your reference number, and if it sits at pending verification beyond about fifteen days, follow up in person.
A clear, complete set of documents on the first try is the single biggest factor in a fast approval.

sections.heading: State-Wise Residency Requirements
rows: Born in UP OR continuous residence 3+ years
Born in Maharashtra OR continuous residence 15+ years
Born in Delhi OR continuous residence 3+ years
Born in Rajasthan OR continuous residence 10+ years (varies by purpose)
Born in MP OR continuous residence 3+ years
Born in Bihar OR continuous residence 5+ years
Born in Karnataka OR continuous residence 10+ years
Native of Tamil Nadu OR continuous residence varies by scheme
Born in Telangana OR residence 7+ years (post 2014 state formation)

sections.heading: Documents You Need
content: For identity, any one of Aadhaar, voter ID, PAN, or passport works, with Aadhaar mandatory in most states. For address, provide any two, such as a ration card, a recent utility bill, or a rent agreement.

To prove continuous residence, school or college certificates, a birth certificate, and voter records are strong. Students applying for the first time should add a transfer certificate and a parent's domicile certificate if available.
If you have recently moved and do not meet the minimum residence period, you cannot get domicile yet. Build up the required years first.
Recent passport-size photographs and a self-declaration or affidavit are also commonly asked for, sometimes on stamp paper.
Keep originals handy for any field verification, since the officer compares them with your uploaded scans.
A school or college certificate from an institution in the state is one of the strongest proofs, since it ties your residence to a fixed period.
Where a document is genuinely missing, affidavits from elderly family members can support your claim during verification.
States that recently formed, like Telangana, often count residence from the formation date, so check how your state measures the period.
Match your name and address exactly across every document, since a single mismatch is enough to delay approval.

sections.heading: How Strong Is Each Proof of Residence
rows: Proves born in state = permanent domicile
Proves registration in state for 6+ months (voter registration takes time)
Proves studied in state - usually 15+ years before certificate date = long residency
Proves current residence (usually 1-2 month old bills dated to showing continuity)
Proves family residence - but can be transferred, so moderate strength
Proves landowner/resident in state for years (land records are permanent)
Must be supported by other documents. Used with voter ID/Aadhaar for confidence.
Proves employment/study in state since certain date

sections.heading: Will your application be approved
qualify: You meet the state's minimum residence period
Name matches across Aadhaar, voter ID, and proofs
You do not hold domicile from another state
You apply in your state of permanent residence
disqualify: Name or address mismatch across documents
Field verification finds you do not live there

sections.heading: Common Reasons for Rejection
content: The most frequent reason is insufficient residence proof that does not clearly show the required continuous period. Add stronger, dated documents that cover the full span.
A document mismatch, where your name or address differs across papers, is next. Make Aadhaar, voter ID, and other proofs read exactly the same.

Holding a valid domicile from another state will get you rejected, as will a failed field verification where neighbours cannot confirm you live there. Fix the stated reason and reapply, with no limit on attempts.
An incomplete application, with a missing field or document, is an avoidable but frequent cause. Check every field before you submit.
When you get a rejection reason, address that exact point and reapply, rather than resending the same papers unchanged.
If your continuous residence falls short of the state's minimum years, the application simply cannot succeed yet, so build the record first.
Blurry or partial document scans also stall verification, so upload clear, complete copies every time.

sections.heading: Where a Domicile Certificate Is Used

items.title: State government jobs
items.sub: State PSC, police, and teaching posts with domicile quotas.

items.title: College quota seats
items.sub: State quota in NEET, engineering, and other admissions.

items.title: Address and KYC proof
items.sub: Supporting proof for some loans and state services.

sections.heading: Domicile for College Admissions
content: The biggest use for young people is state quota seats in professional colleges. In medical and engineering, the state quota cutoff is much lower than the All India Quota.
A NEET score that misses a government seat under All India can still win one under state quota with a valid domicile. You must produce the original certificate at counselling.
Some states add requirements on top, like Maharashtra's caste validity step, so check your state's exact rules before counselling.
The gap between state quota and All India Quota cutoffs is often large, so a domicile certificate can be the single thing that secures a government seat.
Carry the original to counselling, since a provisional or photocopied certificate is frequently not accepted at verification.
Maharashtra and Karnataka layer extra steps on top, so confirm the full document list for your state before the counselling date.
Keep both a printed copy and a DigiLocker version, since portals want an upload and offices often want a hard copy.

sections.heading: Domicile for Government Jobs
content: Almost every state PSC and state-level recruitment needs domicile of that state to claim local quota. State police roles like Sub-Inspector and Constable nearly always require it.
For central jobs like SSC, UPSC, and Railways, domicile is not needed for basic eligibility but may be asked to claim a state quota.
Keep your certificate ready well before any exam deadline, since many candidates lose state quota benefits only because the certificate was not in hand on time.
State teaching and clerical recruitment also lean on domicile, so a candidate without it can be locked out of the local quota entirely.
Treat the certificate as a standing document you renew only if a body demands a fresh one, and keep it ready year-round.

sections.heading: Domicile and Property Purchase
content: In a few states like Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, a domicile certificate matters when buying certain land, since these states restrict purchases by outsiders.
For most ordinary property in most states, you do not need domicile to buy. It comes up mainly for government-allotted land or state housing schemes.
If you are eyeing a state housing subsidy or a PMAY-linked benefit, check whether the scheme asks for domicile before you apply.
Always confirm the exact requirement with the local sub-registrar or the scheme authority, since rules differ sharply between states.
For a normal flat or plot in most states, your sale deed and KYC documents matter far more than a domicile certificate.

sections.title: Validity in Most States
sections.desc:
In most states a domicile certificate has no expiry and stays valid unless you change your permanent state. The Hindi name for it is Niwas Praman Patra.

Some bodies, like the Army or certain universities, still want a fresh certificate issued within the last 6 to 12 months, so check the specific requirement.

sections.heading: Validity, Renewal, and Digital Storage
content: Since most states issue it for life, there is no routine renewal. If your address within the same state changes, the certificate usually stays valid.
Store your certificate on DigiLocker, which most portals and colleges now accept, so you always have a verifiable digital copy.
Keep two or three attested photocopies and a clear scan as well, since some offices still ask for a hard copy.
If a certificate is rejected only for being too old, you reapply for a fresh issuance with updated proofs, rather than renewing the old one.
A DigiLocker copy is treated as legally valid by most institutions, which saves you from carrying papers everywhere.
Treat your domicile certificate as a permanent document you keep safe for years, not something to redo before every application.

sections.heading: Special Cases: Moving, Mixed Records
content: If you were born in one state but lived 20 years in another, you can claim either, by birth in the first or by long residence in the second. Most people apply in their current state.
If you have no birth certificate, an Aadhaar or voter ID from the state plus family records and elder affidavits can still establish domicile.
Land ownership in another state does not override where you actually live. Your domicile is your current state of residence, if you meet its residence period.
Some states waive the residence period for people born there even if they currently live elsewhere, so check your home state's birth-based rule.
When records conflict, a consistent paper trail across Aadhaar, voter ID, and school records is what carries the application through.

sections.title: Apply Online and Apply Early
sections.content:
Apply through your state e-District portal rather than the office. Online applications are tracked with a reference number and usually clear faster.

Start two to three months before any exam or admission deadline, so verification delays never cost you a state quota seat.

sections.title: You Can Hold Only One Domicile
sections.content:
You can have a domicile certificate for only one state at a time. Holding two to claim double benefits is a punishable offence.

If you genuinely change your permanent state, surrender the old certificate before applying for the new one.

sections.text: A domicile certificate is your official proof of state residency - without it, you cannot access state-quota seats in education, government job reservations, or state-specific welfare schemes.

sections.heading: How Much It Costs and How Long It Takes
content: Fees are small in every state, usually between Rs 10 and Rs 100, payable online by UPI, net banking, or card. Some states even issue it free.
Online processing is typically 7 to 15 days, while a Tatkal or express option exists in some states for a faster turnaround.
Apply at least a month or two before any deadline, since field verification and peak admission seasons can stretch the timeline.

sections.heading: Mistakes That Delay Your Certificate
content: The most common slip is choosing the wrong certificate, applying for residence when the college or job actually needs domicile. Read the requirement carefully.
The next is a name or address mismatch across Aadhaar, voter ID, and proofs, which verification flags at once.
Filing too close to a deadline is the third, since field verification needs time. Give yourself a clear buffer of a few weeks.

sections.title: Official Sources and References
sections.content:
This page is based on State Revenue Department rules and the e-District portals, verified against official notifications.

Since domicile rules vary widely by state, always confirm your own state's residence period and portal before applying.

faqs.question: Is domicile certificate valid for lifetime or does it expire?
faqs.answer:
Domicile certificate is valid for lifetime in most states. Once issued, it doesn't expire unless the issuing authority (SDM) explicitly states an expiry date (rare).

However, specific institutions (like NIT/IIT during admission) may prefer recently issued certificates (within 1-2 years). Check the specific requirement of the organization/scheme you're applying to.

faqs.question: I was born in UP but migrated to Tamil Nadu 30 years ago. Which state should I apply for domicile?
faqs.answer:
Apply for Tamil Nadu since you've lived there 30 years (far exceeds TN's requirement of 7 years for most purposes). You can also apply for UP domicile by birth (optional), but for jobs/education in TN, TN domicile is what you need.

Most people apply in their current state of residence.

faqs.question: Can one person have domicile certificates from two states?
faqs.answer:
Technically yes, but practically not recommended. If you apply for domicile in State A and later in State B, you have two valid certificates.

However, for government jobs/education quota, you can use only one domicile at a time. Check the specific job/scheme - it will ask for domicile of that particular state.

Having two creates confusion.

faqs.question: My Aadhaar shows address from 10 years ago but I've lived in current state for 5 years. Will domicile application fail?
faqs.answer:
Possibly. The Patwari will question why your Aadhaar shows old address.

Update your Aadhaar to current address first (₹50, 10-30 days at UIDAI center or online at aadhar.uidai.gov.in). After updating Aadhaar, apply for domicile.

Alternatively, provide other strong evidence (voter ID in new state, current electricity bill, school certificate from current state) along with explanation of address change.

faqs.question: Application under review for 20 days. When will I get certificate?
faqs.answer:
Standard processing is 7-15 days. If pending 20 days, check your portal status: (1) If status shows 'Under Verification', wait till day 15-20.

(2) If status shows 'Pending Documents', contact Patwari immediately with required docs. (3) If no update for 20+ days, visit the SDM office in person with your reference number and ask for status.

Some offices are slow; escalate if needed.

faqs.question: Can I apply for domicile online while currently living abroad?
faqs.answer:
It's complicated. Most e-District portals allow online application submission from anywhere, but verification (Patwari visit, community confirmation) may be delayed or refused if you're not present.

Some states allow family members to collect on your behalf; others require your presence. Best practice: apply before moving abroad or return to your state for verification, then collect certificate.

faqs.question: Domicile certificate certificate says 'Not Valid for Government Employment'. Why?
faqs.answer:
Some states issue limited domicile certificates for specific purposes only (e.g., 'Valid for Educational Quota' but not 'Valid for Government Jobs'). This usually happens when: (1) You requested for a specific purpose, (2) Your residency period is borderline (just meets minimum but not comfortable margin), (3) State's internal restrictions.

If you need unrestricted domicile, apply again specifying 'for all purposes' or contact SDM office explaining why you need expanded scope.

faqs.question: Which documents prove domicile fastest - Voter ID or Aadhaar?
faqs.answer:
Voter ID is slightly stronger as it's official state-level registration. But Aadhaar is now equally strong and more commonly accepted.

Combined (Aadhaar + Voter ID both showing same state address) is the fastest approval. Along with school certificate from that state, approval usually comes in 7-10 days.

Without these, processing extends to 15-20 days.

faqs.question: How long is a domicile certificate valid?
faqs.answer:
In most states, domicile certificates are valid for a lifetime - they don't expire. However, some states issue them with a validity period (3-5 years) and require renewal.

For competitive exam applications, the certificate must be issued before the application deadline. Check your specific state's rules on validity.

faqs.question: Can I get a domicile certificate if I moved to a new state?
faqs.answer:
You need to have resided in the state for a minimum continuous period - typically 10-15 years - to get a domicile certificate. The exact duration varies by state.

If you moved recently, you'll need domicile from your original state. Some states accept domicile from the state where you passed Class 10 or 12, regardless of current residence.

faqs.question: Is a domicile certificate the same as Niwas Praman Patra?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Niwas Praman Patra is simply the Hindi name for a domicile certificate.

Both refer to the same document that proves your permanent residence in a state.

faqs.question: Can married women get domicile of their husband's state?
faqs.answer:
Yes. After marriage, a woman can apply for a domicile certificate of her husband's state based on his residence.

She submits the marriage certificate along with the usual address and identity proofs.

faqs.question: Can I hold a domicile certificate from two states?
faqs.answer:
No, you cannot. You can hold a domicile certificate for only one state at a time, and holding two to claim double benefits is a punishable offence.

If you genuinely shift your permanent state, surrender the old certificate before applying for the new one.

disclaimer: Domicile certificate requirements, procedures, and validity vary significantly by state. This guide reflects common practices as of March 2026. Always verify specific requirements with your state's revenue department or e-District portal.
